items.title: Section: Four Ways a Bodhisattva Works Alongside Others — Including Choosing Rebirth Among Outcastes to Reach Them

items.zh: 有諸菩薩是他同事，而不自顯與他同事；有諸菩薩非他同事，而自顯現與他同事；有諸菩薩是他同事，亦自顯現與他同事；有諸菩薩非他同事，亦不自顯與他同事。第一句者，謂有菩薩與諸菩薩功德威力皆悉平等，於菩薩道自謂為師，功德威力與等菩薩隱自善故，而不顯己功德威力。第二句者，謂諸菩薩，見有下劣信解有情，於甚深處心生怖畏，便正思擇，為欲方便化導彼故，自現己身與其同法。所謂下於旃茶羅類乃至狗類，欲作饒益、欲除災患、欲調、欲化，故思於彼旃茶羅、狗同分中生。第三句者，謂諸菩薩，見所化者所受善根猶可搖動，為令堅住，現與同事或等或增。第四句者，謂諸菩薩自行放逸，棄捨他事。
items.en: There are bodhisattvas who genuinely share another's practice yet do not reveal that they do so; there are bodhisattvas who do not genuinely share another's practice yet outwardly appear to; there are bodhisattvas who both genuinely share another's practice and outwardly appear to; and there are bodhisattvas who neither genuinely share another's practice nor appear to. The first case is a bodhisattva whose own attainment genuinely equals that of the teacher currently instructing a given assembly, who quietly conceals this equal attainment and does not reveal their own accomplishment. The second case is a bodhisattva who, seeing beings of genuinely limited faith and understanding grow frightened at the mere mention of the profound teaching, deliberately takes on a form matching their own circumstances entirely — even choosing rebirth among the lowest castes, or even among dogs, purely in order to benefit them, relieve their suffering, tame them, and guide them. The third case is a bodhisattva who, seeing that a guided being's own wholesome roots remain genuinely unsettled and could still be shaken, visibly matches or even exceeds that being's own practice specifically to help it become genuinely firm. The fourth case is simply a bodhisattva who has become careless, abandoning the work of helping others altogether.

items.zh: 如是已說多種施、戒，廣說乃至最後同事。其中所有波羅蜜多，能自成熟一切佛法；所有攝事，能成熟他一切有情。當知略說菩薩一切善法作業。又如前說多種施、戒，廣說乃至最後同事，如是眾多助菩提分無量善法，由三因緣應知現行，由二因緣應知最勝，由三因緣應知清淨。謂由身語意三因緣故，應知現行。彼諸善法由廣大故、無雜染故，應知最勝。亦名無上、亦名不共。當知此中，由有情無別故、事無別故、時無別故，名為廣大。有情無別者，謂諸菩薩，普於一切有情處所，普為一切法界有情，修行如是施等善根，非專為己。

items.title: Section: What Makes the Six Perfections and Four Means Supreme — Vastness in Every Dimension, and Freedom From Every Contamination

items.zh: 事無別者，謂諸菩薩，普於一切及一切種施等善根精勤受學。時無別者，謂諸菩薩，恒常無間不離加行、不捨善軛，若晝若夜、現法後法，即由此因，施等善根常行無替。當知此中，由四種相成無雜染。謂諸菩薩懷歡喜心修諸善法；由是因緣，無苦、無憂、無諸變悔。又諸菩薩不損惱他、不著見趣、不雜惡行修行施等無量善根。又諸菩薩殷重遍體，於其施等無量善法唯見功德、唯見真實、唯見寂靜，極善決定，不從他緣、非餘引奪而正受學。又諸菩薩不因所修施等善法悕異熟果，或轉輪王、或天帝釋、或魔、或梵；亦不於他悕求返報。無所依止，不依一切利養恭敬世俗名譽，乃至不依養活身命。
items.en: No partiality among practices means bodhisattvas diligently take up and study every single kind and category of generosity and the rest, without favouring one over another. No interruption across time means bodhisattvas, constantly and without any gap, never departing from actual practice and never setting down the yoke of wholesome effort, whether by day or by night, in this life or lives to come — through this cause, their practice of generosity and the rest continues constantly without ever being replaced by anything else. One should know that freedom from contamination is accomplished through four further marks. Bodhisattvas cultivate every wholesome practice with a genuinely joyful mind; through this cause, they experience no suffering, no anxiety, and no regretful wavering in it. Bodhisattvas likewise cultivate boundless wholesome roots of generosity and the rest without harming any being, without attachment to any rival view, and without any admixture of unwholesome conduct. Bodhisattvas cultivate these practices with genuine, thoroughgoing seriousness, seeing in generosity and the rest only genuine merit, only genuine truth, only genuine peace, holding this with settled, decisive conviction that comes from within, never borrowed from another and never able to be shaken loose by any other influence. And bodhisattvas do not cultivate generosity and the rest hoping for any karmic reward — becoming a universal monarch, the ruler of the gods, Māra, or the great god Brahma — nor do they seek any repayment from those they help; they rely on nothing at all, neither on others' material support, reverence, or worldly reputation, nor even on securing their own livelihood.

items.zh: 由如是相淨歡喜俱、無不平等、殷重、無依，修行施等，廣說乃至同事為後無量善法，名無雜染。

items.title: Section: Blazing Yet Unshaken, Growing Like the Waxing Moon — Closing the Six Perfections and Four Means as One Unified Activity

items.zh: 由熾然故、無動轉故、善清淨故，應知清淨。若諸菩薩已入清淨意樂地者，一切善根熾然無動。言熾然者，謂此菩薩意樂淨故，一切善法不由思擇，熾盛現前。言無動者，謂此菩薩意樂淨故，隨所獲得、隨所積集所有善法皆無退轉，於當來世能無退減。如是菩薩，隨所經歷彼彼日夜、隨所過度彼彼自身，所有善法如明分月，唯增無減。若諸菩薩住到究竟地、或繫屬一生最後有者，所有善法名善清淨。此上更無菩薩地攝勝淨法故。如是施等同事為後無量善法，三因緣故應知現行，二因緣故應知最勝，三因緣故應知清淨。
items.en: Through blazing forth, through remaining unshaken, and through being genuinely well purified, one should understand purity itself. Bodhisattvas who have already entered the ground of genuinely pure aspiration find every wholesome root blazing forth spontaneously, unshaken. "Blazing forth" means that, this bodhisattva's aspiration being genuinely pure, every wholesome practice manifests vigorously without needing deliberate reflection to bring it about. "Unshaken" means that, this bodhisattva's aspiration being genuinely pure, every wholesome quality already attained and accumulated never regresses, and will never diminish in any future life either. Such a bodhisattva, across every day and night that passes, across every successive lifetime lived, finds these wholesome qualities only ever increasing, like the moon waxing towards fullness, never diminishing. Bodhisattvas who abide having reached the ultimate ground, or who are bound to one more life in their final existence, possess wholesome qualities that are called genuinely, completely purified — beyond this point, there remains no further supreme purity within the bodhisattva stages left to attain. In this way, generosity and the rest, including working alongside others as their final member, together constitute boundless wholesome practice: manifesting through three causes, supreme through two, and pure through three, as should now be understood.

blocks.text: How bodhisattvas share others' lives, and what makes the perfections supreme. A passage (0532b09) is untranslated.

Some bodhisattvas share another's practice but don't reveal it; some appear to share it but don't; some both; some neither. And some choose rebirth among outcasts to reach them. Venerable Miào Jìng: a bodhisattva who fails to share practice may have lost the resolve.

The perfections ripen one's own Buddha qualities; the means of embracing ripen all other beings: together, "a bodhisattva's whole work of goodness". These practices operate through body, speech, and mind; they are supreme because they are vast and undefiled; and pure for three reasons. "Vast" means without distinction of beings (practised "for all beings throughout the Dharma realm, not for oneself alone"), of things, or of time.

"No partiality among practices": every kind of giving and the rest. "No interruption across time." And "bodhisattvas do not practise generosity and the rest hoping for any reward: becoming a universal monarch, Śakra, Māra, or Brahmā". Master Cháng Bǎi explains those rebirths.

"Through blazing forth, remaining unshaken, and being well purified, one understands purity." For bodhisattvas who have entered the ground of pure intention (Venerable Miào Jìng: the Ground of Joy), "their wholesome qualities, like the moon in its waxing half, only increase and never diminish". Master Cháng Bǎi: like the moon from the first to the fifteenth.

quiz.q: The fourth case: "neither working alongside nor appearing to" — "the bodhisattva is careless and abandons others." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: this must be an ordinary or provisions-stage bodhisattva who has lost bodhicitta; Cháng Bǎi: because they became careless, they don't appear to work alongside either
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this bodhisattva must be at the ordinary or provisions stage — it is because bodhicitta has been lost. Master Cháng Bǎi: because they have become careless, they also do not show themselves working alongside others.

quiz.q: One mark of freedom from contamination: what do bodhisattvas not hope for from their wholesome practice?
options: ripened rewards such as being a wheel-turning king, Śakra, Māra, or Brahmā — nor repayment from others
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas do not practise generosity and the rest hoping for any karmic reward — becoming a universal monarch, Śakra, Māra, or Brahmā — nor do they seek any repayment." Venerable Miào Jìng: "without reliance" simply means seeking nothing.

quiz.q: The English renders "mó" as "a heavenly king." How do the lectures explain it?
options: Māra, king of the sixth desire-realm heaven; Brahmā is the great Brahmā of the first absorption
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Māra king of the sixth desire-realm heaven, or the great Brahmā king of the first absorption. Venerable Miào Jìng: becoming Māra king at the top of the six desire heavens. The English "a heavenly king" should be Māra.

quiz.q: For bodhisattvas who have entered the ground of pure aspiration, what are their wholesome qualities like?
options: like the waxing moon — only increasing, never diminishing
quiz.why: "Their wholesome qualities, like the moon in its waxing half, only increase and never diminish." Master Cháng Bǎi: like the moon from the first to the fifteenth, only brighter, never less. Venerable Miào Jìng: each month has a dark half and a bright half.

quiz.q: "Bodhisattvas who have entered the ground of pure aspiration" — which ground is this, according to the lectures?
options: the Ground of Joy — the first ground
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the ground of pure aspiration is the Ground of Joy. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the Ground of Great Joy; there the six perfections and four means arise spontaneously without deliberate effort.
